facility: Sacramento County Probation Department, Youth Detention Facility
provenance: **This is not the whole order. It is the provisions that change.** The order runs to twelve pages and was produced and read in full in Revision 9, but the PDF did not survive the container it was read in. What survives is every provision quoted at the time, word for word, and those are reproduced below. Everything between them is not reproduced and is marked as such. Each provision says whether its text is the order's own words or a description from the register, and a redline is shown only where the words are the order's.
not_reproduced: Eleven of the order's twelve pages are not reproduced here. That includes the Purpose and Scope paragraph, the S-1, S-2, S-3, S-5, S-6 and S-7 criteria, the III.E housing matrix in full, the III.D deviation rules, section IV on legal status changes, and section V. None of them is amended by changes 1 or 6, but their absence is why this document cannot be handed over as the order. **To produce a complete tracked changes copy of OO 1352, the PDF has to be uploaded again.** That is a single step and it would take about an hour.

provisions.label: Change 1. Rescind the S-8 classification
provisions.status_note: Verified in Revision 9 against the order as produced. The order's own words, including subparagraph a.
runs: del

Any Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, Questioning and Intersex (LGBTQI) youth to further protect against victimization/discrimination within the unit setting. a. See the Transgender and Intersex Youth Policy for housing guidelines.
ins
Prohibited bases for separation and single occupancy assignment.
sub: Staff shall not separate a youth from the general population, and shall not assign a youth to a single occupancy room, based solely on the youth's actual or perceived race, ethnic group identification, ancestry, national origin, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, immigration status, mental or physical disability, or medical condition.

Nothing in this section prohibits placing a youth in a single occupancy room at the youth's own specific request, or in accordance with the separation provisions of this order, OO 1354, and OO 1354.5. A request under this paragraph shall be documented in JPIP with the date, the substance of the request, and the staff member who received it.

Where a youth's sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression is known to staff, that information shall be used as one input to the individualized housing determination required by OO 1352.5 III.B and III.F. It shall not by itself determine a housing assignment, a program assignment, or a classification code.
No classification code shall be created or maintained whose assignment carries an automatic housing consequence on any basis listed in paragraph 1.

provisions.action: Remove every S-8 row and column from the III.E housing matrix, and remove S-8 from the JPIP classification code table, the classification worksheet, and any intake screen that offers it, so the code cannot be assigned after the order is amended. Without that step the order changes and the practice does not.

before_adoption: **This document shows the provisions that change, not the order.** It cannot be circulated as a copy of OO 1352, and it is not a substitute for amending the order itself. Upload the PDF and a complete tracked changes version can be built the same way the OO 1453 one was.

**Two provisions carry no redline because their words are not held.** The III.E housing matrix and II.C.3 are marked as described rather than quoted, and each states the action required instead of showing struck text. Do not let either be read as though the wording had been checked.

**Change 1 replaces II.M in place rather than striking it**, so the balance of section II does not need renumbering. The replacement tracks the 15 CCR 1352(e) list and carries the regulation's own carve-out, single occupancy at the youth's specific request, documented. Paragraph 4 is the one that stops S-8 reappearing under a different letter.

**The operational half of change 1 is not in the text.** Removing the code from the order does nothing for a youth already carrying it. Re-determining housing for every current S-8 youth, within a stated number of days and documented, is what makes the amendment real.

**Penal Code 261.5, 288.5 and 289.6 in the S-4A offence list are the drafter's judgment**, not sections the order enumerates and not sections this review has verified as the right additions. Only 287 and 289 are confirmed omissions, recorded against the order's own enumeration at II.G.1 and II.G.3. The other three come from the drafted amendment at change 6 and carry the same status there. Confirm all three with County Counsel, or strike them and keep the successor-statute catch-all, which is what stops the next renumbering reopening the gap that 287 left.

**This review found the Purpose and Scope paragraph of OO 1352, PREA Policy III.E, and OO 1352.5 III.H already state the correct rule.** The amendment brings II.M and III.I into line with three provisions the department has already written correctly, which is worth saying when the change is put to anyone.
